raw_response:
I farm 10.1 mu in a wheat-maize rotation with only two people in the household, and some labor is tied up off-farm, so I will keep the system simple, reliable, and not too labor-intensive. Because I have 30 years of farming experience, good education, and access to well irrigation, I will lean on improved seed, moderate-to-high input use, and timely water rather than low-input risk-taking. For wheat, I will aim for a stable stand, enough nitrogen to support yield, balanced phosphorus for roots, some potassium for stress resistance, and a few irrigations at the key stages. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want stronger yield potential, then push fertilizer a bit higher than wheat and rely on fewer but timely irrigations because summer rain can help. I will use rotary tillage because it fits a small farm, saves labor compared with deep ploughing every season, and works well in this rotation. I will keep pesticide use moderate and targeted because I want to protect yield without doing unnecessary sprays.
